source.articleTitle: The Influence of Residual Feed Intake and Cow Age on Beef Cattle Performance, Supplement Intake, Resource Use, and Grazing Behavior on Winter Mixed-Grass Rangelands
source.licenseEvidence: The article states that it and its materials are distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license; the data are the article's Supplementary Tables S1-S5.
source.population: Non-lactating, pregnant commercial Angus cows, ages 1-10 years, on dormant mixed-grass rangeland in Montana across two grazing years.

Table S2.csv.purpose: Individual daily supplement intake and feeder behavior

Table S3.csv.purpose: GPS subset daily grazing time and distance

caveats: Table S1 rows are cow-season records, not 408 unique cows.
ADG is derived as period body-weight change divided by the article-reported 84-day grazing period; it is not a daily time series.
Supplement intake is not total forage dry-matter intake.
The cohort is a separate U.S. pregnant Angus population and is not the USDA/CPER observational cohort.
The article describes observational associations with age and RFI; this dataset does not identify causal effects of grazing or supplementation.
